r0.why: Definition with protein/functional RNA [1], range of functions [4], continuous vs regulated expression [5].

r1.why: Multiple steps incl. transcription [2],[6], translation to amino-acid chain that folds [3], RNA itself as product for non-coding [3],[45].

r2.why: One ribonucleotide at a time by complementarity [6], U replaces T [7], single bacterial polymerase [8], three eukaryotic in nucleus with promoter and TFs [9], terminator [13].

r3.why: Prokaryotic mRNA ready vs eukaryotic transcript needing modification [14], 5' cap protects from degradation [17], 3' cleavage and ~200 A poly(A) tail protects [19],[21].

r4.why: Exons/introns [25], spliceosome removes intron and joins exons [26], introns/exons retained or removed [27], alternative transcripts and proteins [28],[29].

r5.why: Together in prokaryotes, nuclear membrane separates giving processing time [31], possible evolutionary advantage of nucleus [30].
